fields: What should drive Claude model selection?
Measured workload requirements across quality, latency, cost, tool use, context needs, and risk.
Why should model names not be hard-coded as permanent architecture assumptions?
Model lineups have lifecycle states and change over time.
What should happen after changing the model in production?
Re-run workload-specific regression, latency, safety, and cost evaluations.
What is the role of a system prompt in architecture?
To provide trusted behavioral instructions, scope, constraints, and output expectations.
Why is a system prompt not an authorization boundary?
Model compliance is probabilistic; protected actions need enforceable controls outside the model.
How should untrusted retrieved/user content be handled relative to trusted instructions?
Keep it structurally separated and do not allow it to silently redefine policy.
When should few-shot examples be added?
When representative examples measurably improve ambiguous behavior, formatting, tone, or boundary cases.
What is zero-shot prompting?
Giving clear task instructions without examples.
What is the key principle of context engineering?
Put the smallest useful set of high-signal information in the model's active context for the current decision.
Why is more context not automatically better?
Irrelevant or stale context consumes tokens and can compete with relevant information.
What content is a strong candidate for prompt reuse/caching?
Large stable instructions or reference material reused across many requests.
What content is a poor caching candidate?
Frequently changing transactional state that must be current.
Active model
A fully supported model recommended for current use.
Deprecated model
A model still functional for a period but no longer recommended and scheduled for retirement.
Behavioral instruction
Prompt guidance that influences how the model should act.
Enforceable control
Code, permissions, schema, policy, or approval logic that guarantees a boundary outside model compliance.
Zero-shot
Clear direct instructions without worked examples.
Few-shot / multishot
Representative examples included to demonstrate desired behavior.
Active context
Information currently visible to the model for the present inference.
Compaction
Compressing a long interaction into a smaller representation that preserves important state and decisions.
Prompt template
Reusable stable prompt structure with request-specific variables.
Choose the model that meets the workload's {{c1::quality threshold}} at acceptable latency and cost.
Model migration should be treated as a {{c1::production change}} and re-evaluated.
Use prompts to guide behavior; use {{c1::deterministic controls}} to enforce hard security and policy invariants.
Keep trusted instructions structurally separate from {{c1::untrusted user or retrieved content}}.
If a clear zero-shot prompt already passes the eval, extra examples may add {{c1::unnecessary tokens and maintenance}}.
Prompt engineering should respond to {{c1::observed evaluation failures}}, not ritual complexity.
The context window should be treated as a finite {{c1::working set}}, not a database.
Large corpora are often better handled with {{c1::just-in-time retrieval}} than by preloading everything.
Reuse is safest when the content is {{c1::stable enough}} that freshness is not compromised.
Agent Skills use {{c1::progressive disclosure}} so detailed resources can load only when relevant.
What lifecycle state follows Active in the documented set Active, Legacy, Deprecated, Retired?
Legacy
What should compare candidate models on the real workload rather than generic reputation?
Evaluation suite
What prompt layer should hold stable high-trust behavioral instructions?
System prompt
What should enforce authorization rather than relying on the model?
Deterministic control
What prompting technique provides representative examples?
Few-shot prompting
What structured markup style can separate instructions, context, and examples in complex Claude prompts?
XML tags
What technique summarizes a long trace while preserving critical state?
Compaction
What Anthropic mechanism packages reusable instructions, scripts, and resources for agents?
Agent Skills
A routine classifier passes all quality thresholds on a faster model while a stronger model costs much more. What is the best choice?

[{"id":"a","text":"Use the faster model for that workload unless other constraints justify the stronger model."},{"id":"b","text":"Always use the strongest model."},{"id":"c","text":"Always use the cheapest model even if it fails quality."},{"id":"d","text":"Route randomly between models."}]
a
Model choice is a workload-specific trade-off, not a prestige decision.
A model is being retired. What should the team do before switching to its replacement?

[{"id":"a","text":"Run task-specific regression, safety, latency, and cost evaluation."},{"id":"b","text":"Assume the newer model is behaviorally identical."},{"id":"c","text":"Only compare benchmark scores."},{"id":"d","text":"Change the model without testing because the API shape is similar."}]
a
Model migration can change behavior and should be evaluated.
A workflow has easy classification cases and rare complex exceptions. What design may improve economics if validated?

[{"id":"a","text":"Route routine cases to a fast model and difficult cases to a stronger model."},{"id":"b","text":"Use the strongest model for every request by default."},{"id":"c","text":"Use the cheapest model for every request regardless of errors."},{"id":"d","text":"Remove evaluation and route by input length only."}]
a
Evaluated routing can match model capability to workload difficulty.
Which evidence is strongest for choosing between two Claude models for a production task?

[{"id":"a","text":"Results on a representative eval suite for that task plus latency/cost measurements."},{"id":"b","text":"A generic leaderboard alone."},{"id":"c","text":"Which model name sounds newer."},{"id":"d","text":"A single anecdotal prompt."}]
a
Architecture should use representative workload evidence.
A refund policy says amounts over $500 require manager approval. What is the strongest implementation?

[{"id":"a","text":"Explain the rule in the prompt and enforce the threshold in deterministic approval logic."},{"id":"b","text":"Put the rule only in the system prompt."},{"id":"c","text":"Use a longer example showing a $499 refund."},{"id":"d","text":"Ask the model to self-check twice."}]
a
Prompts guide behavior; protected thresholds need enforceable controls.
Retrieved documents may contain malicious instructions. What prompt design is strongest?

[{"id":"a","text":"Clearly separate untrusted retrieved content from trusted instructions and restrict capabilities independently."},{"id":"b","text":"Concatenate all text into one unstructured prompt."},{"id":"c","text":"Tell retrieved text it is trusted."},{"id":"d","text":"Rely on the model to always ignore injections."}]
a
Trust boundaries should be explicit and backed by controls.
Downstream software requires valid structured output. What should the architecture add?

[{"id":"a","text":"An explicit output contract plus schema validation."},{"id":"b","text":"Only ask for JSON politely."},{"id":"c","text":"Increase temperature."},{"id":"d","text":"Remove the system prompt."}]
a
Structure should be specified and validated when machines depend on it.
A team wants reusable prompts with changing request data. Which design is best?

[{"id":"a","text":"Keep stable instructions in a template and inject request-specific variables separately."},{"id":"b","text":"Copy-paste a new giant prompt for every request."},{"id":"c","text":"Put all user data into the system policy section."},{"id":"d","text":"Mix examples, policy, and untrusted data without structure."}]
a
Templates separate stable instructions from variable content.
A classifier confuses two boundary cases even with clear instructions. What is a strong next step?

[{"id":"a","text":"Add a few representative examples that demonstrate the boundary distinction and re-evaluate."},{"id":"b","text":"Add dozens of irrelevant examples."},{"id":"c","text":"Switch to an agent immediately."},{"id":"d","text":"Hide the labels from the prompt."}]
a
Few-shot examples are useful when they target observed ambiguity.
A straightforward extraction task already meets its quality target zero-shot. What should the team do?

[{"id":"a","text":"Keep the simpler prompt unless evaluation identifies a failure."},{"id":"b","text":"Add chain-of-thought instructions automatically."},{"id":"c","text":"Add ten examples for safety."},{"id":"d","text":"Create a multi-agent workflow."}]
a
Use the lightest technique that passes the evaluation.
A long prompt mixes policy, examples, retrieved text, and user data. What improvement is most direct?

[{"id":"a","text":"Structure the prompt so trusted instructions, examples, context, and inputs are clearly separated."},{"id":"b","text":"Increase temperature."},{"id":"c","text":"Repeat every instruction three times."},{"id":"d","text":"Remove all examples regardless of performance."}]
a
Clear structure reduces ambiguity about the role of each section.
A retrieval system is returning the wrong document. What is the least promising first response?

[{"id":"a","text":"Endlessly rewrite the prompt without fixing retrieval."},{"id":"b","text":"Inspect retrieval results."},{"id":"c","text":"Evaluate chunking/ranking."},{"id":"d","text":"Correct the retrieval layer."}]
a
Prompting cannot compensate for missing or wrong evidence indefinitely.
An agent preloads thousands of pages although each task uses only a few. What is the strongest change?

[{"id":"a","text":"Retrieve relevant content just in time instead of preloading the corpus."},{"id":"b","text":"Increase prompt verbosity."},{"id":"c","text":"Duplicate the corpus in conversation history."},{"id":"d","text":"Always use multiple agents."}]
a
JIT retrieval preserves context for relevant information.
A long-running agent approaches practical context limits. What should compaction preserve?

[{"id":"a","text":"Key decisions, constraints, unresolved work, and important evidence."},{"id":"b","text":"Every raw tool response verbatim."},{"id":"c","text":"Only the last user message."},{"id":"d","text":"Nothing; simply drop all prior state."}]
a
Compaction reduces size while preserving decision-critical information.
Two independent research tasks pollute each other's context. What pattern can help?

[{"id":"a","text":"Use context isolation with separate workers/subagents."},{"id":"b","text":"Merge all transcripts into one prompt."},{"id":"c","text":"Increase temperature."},{"id":"d","text":"Cache every tool result forever."}]
a
Separate contexts reduce interference between independent workstreams.
A team stores the only copy of an order's authoritative state in conversation history. What is wrong?

[{"id":"a","text":"Application state should live in an authoritative external store, not depend on the model context."},{"id":"b","text":"Conversation history is always more durable than databases."},{"id":"c","text":"The context should be made longer."},{"id":"d","text":"Only the system prompt needs changing."}]
a
Model context is a working set, not durable system state.
A legal workflow reuses the same large policy manual for thousands of requests. What is a strong optimization?

[{"id":"a","text":"Reuse/cache the stable reference content while fetching case-specific current state separately."},{"id":"b","text":"Cache each client's live case status indefinitely."},{"id":"c","text":"Duplicate the manual into every variable section."},{"id":"d","text":"Remove freshness checks from current data."}]
a
Stable repeated context is a good reuse target; volatile state is not.
A shared Skill changes how production agents perform a regulated workflow. How should it be managed?

[{"id":"a","text":"Version, review, test, and control changes like other operational assets."},{"id":"b","text":"Treat it as harmless prose with no review."},{"id":"c","text":"Let every user edit it globally."},{"id":"d","text":"Never regression-test Skill changes."}]
a
Reusable agent instructions/resources can change behavior and should be governed.
Which data is the worst prompt-caching candidate?

[{"id":"a","text":"A user's current account balance that changes frequently."},{"id":"b","text":"A stable policy manual."},{"id":"c","text":"A fixed system instruction block."},{"id":"d","text":"A reusable set of examples."}]
a
Caching must not undermine freshness for live state.
A huge Skill library exists, but only one Skill is relevant per task. What design principle helps?

[{"id":"a","text":"Progressive disclosure/loading of the relevant Skill details."},{"id":"b","text":"Load every Skill in full on every request."},{"id":"c","text":"Disable Skills entirely."},{"id":"d","text":"Store live transactional state inside every Skill."}]
a
Progressive disclosure limits context to relevant reusable expertise.

Order a sound model-selection process.

[{"id":"s1","text":"Define task quality and operational thresholds"},{"id":"s2","text":"Evaluate candidate models on representative cases"},{"id":"s3","text":"Compare quality, latency, cost, and risk"},{"id":"s4","text":"Select the model/routing policy"},{"id":"s5","text":"Re-test when the model or workload changes"}]
Requirements and evaluation precede selection; changes trigger re-evaluation.
Order a secure prompt-to-action pattern.

[{"id":"s1","text":"Establish trusted system instructions"},{"id":"s2","text":"Insert user/retrieved content as untrusted data"},{"id":"s3","text":"Let the model propose an output/action"},{"id":"s4","text":"Validate schema and authorization deterministically"},{"id":"s5","text":"Execute only if controls pass"}]
Behavioral prompting precedes deterministic validation and execution.
Order an evidence-driven prompt-improvement loop.

[{"id":"s1","text":"Establish a simple baseline prompt"},{"id":"s2","text":"Run representative evaluations"},{"id":"s3","text":"Identify a specific failure mode"},{"id":"s4","text":"Apply the lightest targeted prompting change"},{"id":"s5","text":"Re-run evaluation and regression checks"}]
Prompt complexity should be added in response to observed failures.
Order a long-horizon context-management approach.

[{"id":"s1","text":"Keep authoritative state externally"},{"id":"s2","text":"Retrieve only information relevant to the current step"},{"id":"s3","text":"Work within the active context"},{"id":"s4","text":"Compact older interactions when needed"},{"id":"s5","text":"Reload external state/evidence for later decisions"}]
External state and JIT context keep the working set bounded over time.
Order a safe prompt-reuse decision.

[{"id":"s1","text":"Identify repeated context"},{"id":"s2","text":"Determine whether it is stable enough to reuse"},{"id":"s3","text":"Separate volatile request/user state"},{"id":"s4","text":"Cache or package the stable portion"},{"id":"s5","text":"Invalidate or bypass reuse when freshness changes"}]
Reuse follows stability analysis and must preserve freshness.
